objective: Make the upstream-report structure check refuse a status outside the package's own vocabulary and a false pass field, so a renamed or self-declared field cannot read as a valid upstream approval.
decision_supported: Does a non-empty status string plus a boolean pass field prove an upstream package is structurally valid, or does the check need the package's own vocabulary and a true result?
acceptance: A status outside the package's declared vocabulary fails the structure check.
A false pass or engineering_package_pass fails it; the field has to be true.
A missing pass field fails it.
Every package in UPSTREAM_REPORTS has a declared vocabulary, and its committed status is in it.
The committed reports still pass the structure check.
The check is still per-package: a ready status belonging to another package is refused.
The regenerated release report records the two new checks and still passes.
evidence: Before the change, setting the PCB status to JUST_A_STRING with the staged blocks removed left every structural check passing.
Before the change, setting pass to False with the staged blocks removed also left every check passing; only an unrelated staged-consistency check happened to catch the combined mutation.
After the change those two mutations fail on status_is_in_the_package_vocabulary and structural_pass_field_is_true respectively, and the committed reports still pass.
Regenerating the release report adds status_is_in_the_package_vocabulary and structural_pass_field_is_true to every upstream entry, both true.
stop_conditions: A package legitimately reports a status not in its vocabulary; that status has to be added to UPSTREAM_STATUSES, which is where a reviewer sees it.
risks_and_fallbacks: Adding a status now requires editing the table, which is deliberate friction on a release vocabulary.
The check still does not bind the report to an input digest; that is a separate issue.
